question: Which REDMI Watch 6 3.100.043 entries are the NuttX VFS, app-registry and page-manager functions the staged Supervisor needs?
method: Manual review of the exact 3.100.043 IDB (fwbins/xiaomi-p65-3.100.043/vela_ap.bin.i64, sha256 a19b6014…5858): each entry was decompiled and checked against the reviewed 3.1.28/3.1.190 semantics, its assert/log string, and its callee shapes. Addresses are the SRAM/PSRAM-resident bodies; several XIP copies are thunks (`0xc8beaf0 -> 0x1c158720`, `0xc8bef00 -> 0x1c1580e4`).

findings.name: open
findings.anchor: va_list path resolution (sub_1C157D24, 'vfs/fs_open.c'), fd allocation sub_1C154300, errno set through sub_1C168478. Sibling 0x1c158074 is the same path without the errno store.

findings.name: close
findings.anchor: file table lookup (inode/fs_files.c:1006 assert), fd range check, reference decrement and last-reference release.

findings.name: read
findings.anchor: 'vfs/fs_read.c' assert at line 70, fs_getfilep 0x1c154700, readable-flag check, dispatch through inode->ops[+8] (file_read 0x1c158790), errno on failure.

findings.name: write
findings.anchor: Same wrapper shape as read: fs_getfilep 0x1c154700, writable-flag check, dispatch through inode->ops[+12] (file_write 0x1c159a90), errno on failure.

findings.name: unlink
findings.anchor: 'vfs/fs_unlink.c' assert; path lookup, inode type checks, driver/mount unlink dispatch, inode_lock 0x1c154f50 + fs_inoderemove 0x1c1557b4 + unlock.

findings.name: rename
findings.anchor: 'vfs/fs_rename.c' assertions in the two-path resolution body.

findings.name: errno_location
findings.anchor: Returns TLS pointer +40 or the static errno slot 0x3c3e... — the NuttX get_errno_ptr shape; every libc wrapper above stores through it.

findings.name: app_lookup
findings.anchor: Walks the registered-app list at off_3C3CF91C comparing the 16-bit app id at +16; returns the descriptor or 0.

findings.name: app_install
findings.anchor: 'app_install' log tag; copies the 64-byte descriptor, clones strings, appends to off_3C3CF91C, allocates and registers the page array, emits event 27.

findings.name: page_goto
findings.anchor: 'pagemanager' / 'goto_page_no_check_stacktop' log strings; page-stack lookup and transition through sub_1C132B7C/sub_1C13218C.

findings.name: page_finish
findings.anchor: 'finish_page' log string; page-stack top handling and release.

findings.name: register_driver
findings.anchor: inode_lock, inode_reserve(path, mode, &node) 0x1c155888, fops stored at +16, type bits at +14 set to 1, private data at +24, unlock. Four arguments (path, fops, mode, private); the mode reaches inode_reserve, which does not consume it in this build.

findings.name: unregister_driver
findings.anchor: inode_lock + fs_inoderemove(path) 0x1c1557b4 + unlock.

findings.name: lv_obj_class_create_obj
findings.anchor: lv_obj_class.c assertions ('lv_obj_class_create_obj', 'No display created yet. No place to assign the new screen'); the class create occurs here, the init is 0x3776b0.

findings.name: lv_obj_class_init_obj
findings.anchor: called immediately after 0x3775bc by every widget create; base class 0x3c1de5c8.

findings.name: lv_obj_create
findings.anchor: create helper with class 0x3c1de5c8 (base_class 0 = lv_obj_class) + init; followed by the lv_obj_class.c path string.

findings.name: lv_label_create
findings.anchor: create helper with class 0x3c224844; the same class struct appears in XIP rodata at 0xc3145b8 immediately before the lv_label.c source path and the 'Failed to allocate memory for dot_tmp_ptr' label string.

findings.name: mpu_region_allocate
findings.anchor: BES region allocator over the 8-bit bitmap algn_3C489EAC, IRQ-masked, 255 when full.

findings.name: mpu_region_configure
findings.anchor: Five-argument configure(region<=7, base 32-aligned, size>0x1F, access<=5, lock) computing RBAR/RLAR and writing RNR/RBAR/RLAR (0xE000ED98/9C/A0) through 0xc9665a0; called by the alloc-and-configure mpu_setup 0xc9666b0.

findings.name: mpu_region_release
findings.anchor: Clears the bitmap bit for region<=7; the caller disables the hardware region (RNR/RLAR=0), which is what stage1 and the Supervisor unmap path do.

findings.name: default heap
findings.anchor: BES heap wrappers over the descriptor stored at 0x3c3d7e9c (dword_3C3D4F10[3043]); Mirage reads that slot as 0x3c57f980, i.e. the default heap lives in PSRAM - a Supervisor image allocated there executes through the 0x1c alias, so the p65 loader follows the Band 11 design (alias + explicit MPU lease), not the SRAM-resident Band 9 one.

limits: Static review only: device is NOT_PROBED and no capability is claimed.
read/write/unlink/rename are the SRAM-resident originals; the XIP copies are thunks and must not be recorded as separate callables.
register_driver keeps the four-argument NuttX signature; a three-argument veneer call would leave private data undefined.
lv_memalign/lv_free wrappers over the default heap descriptor 0x3c3d4f10[3043] are located (0xc50b2c8 / 0xc50b25c) but not yet recorded.
The remaining LVGL setters (label text, image src, bar range/value, size, align, flags, event) and the image/bar create helpers are not resolved yet.
